newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may build oil link around Chechnya - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia may build oil link around Chechnya - agency.

text.p: Russia may build a section of oil pipeline around its independence-minded republic of Chechnya because of problems in sealing an oil transport deal with the separatist region, a senior energy official said on Wednesday.

First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko, quoted by Interfax news agency, said it would take 1-1/2 to two years and $250 million to replace 160 km of pipeline running through Chechnya with a new stretch through a neighbouring region, Dagestan.
The section of pipeline through Chechnya is part of a trunk pipeline linking the Azeri capital Baku and Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet of Novorossiisk.

The $8 billion, 13-member Azerbaijan International Operating Company, or AIOC, led by British Petroleum and Statoil, is scheduled to use the Baku-Novorossiisk link to send its Caspian oil to world markets.
But Moscow is having problems hammering out an agreement with Chechnya over refurbishing the link and other prickly issues.
Moscow sent troops into Chechnya in December 1994 to try to crush an independence drive, but it withdrew in humiliation last August after a bitter, 21-month war.

Some agreements have been signed to allow AIOC to use the pipeline, but not all issues have been resolved, including the delicate matter of how much money Chechnya may earn in transit fees for sending oil across its section of the link.

AIOC is to start production on August 28 at its Caspian fields but will not need the pipeline until the end of December. Russia has said it will take about 20 days and $2 million to refurbish the existing link running through Chechnya.
